note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in MA.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Battle Road
byways.designation: Massachusetts Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway (FHWA, 2021)
byways.where: Massachusetts Ave and North Great Rd (Route 2A) from Tufts St, Arlington, through Lexington and Lincoln to Monument St, Concord; Middlesex County

facts.fact: The byway is about 14 miles long, running from Tufts Street and Massachusetts Avenue in Arlington along Massachusetts Avenue and North Great Road to Concord, ending at the Buttrick Mansion and Muster Field in Minute Man National Historical Park.
It follows the approximate path of the British regulars during the fighting of April 19, 1775, and was designated a state scenic byway in November 2006.
FHWA lists it as a National Scenic Byway, 16 miles, in Arlington, Lexington, Lincoln and Concord.

byways.review: State act and MAPC give 6 Nov 2006 and 8 Nov 2006 (Chapter 345 of the Acts of 2006) for designation; FHWA designated it national in 2021 (FHWA id 81503).

byways.name: Blackstone Canal Heritage Highway
byways.where: Route 122 from Millbury and Grafton through Northbridge, Uxbridge and Millville to the Rhode Island line at Blackstone; Worcester County

facts.fact: Route 122 in Massachusetts is known as the Blackstone Canal Heritage Highway and passes through many of the valley's mill villages.
Route 122 follows the Blackstone River through Blackstone and Millville, crosses it in Uxbridge and again in northern Northbridge.
The Blackstone Canal linked Worcester and Providence; it opened in 1828 and shut down in 1848.

byways.review: No official byway page found. MassDOT's 2018 map describes it as the Worcester-Providence corridor through the Blackstone River Valley National Heritage Corridor; Scenic America calls it 'Blackstone Canal Heritage Byway'.

byways.name: Chappaquiddick Road
byways.where: Chappaquiddick Road from Chappy Point across Chappaquiddick Island, Edgartown; Dukes County

facts.fact: Chappaquiddick is an island off the eastern end of Martha's Vineyard, administratively part of Edgartown.

Chappaquiddick Road and Poucha Road are paved and give access to sandy woodland roads, trails and shorelines; the island has red cedar woods and salt marshes, and visitors come for the Mytoi Gardens, a small Japanese garden in the native brush.
MassDOT's byway map describes the route as winding along the island's coast to the point, with views of the smaller of the Vineyard islands.

byways.review: No official page found. MassDOT line is about 3.9 mi of centerline segments.

byways.name: Connecticut River Scenic Farm Byway
byways.designation: Massachusetts Scenic Byway; Massachusetts section of the Connecticut River Byway National Scenic Byway
byways.where: Routes 47 and 63 from South Hadley through Hadley, Sunderland and Montague to Northfield; Hampshire and Franklin counties

facts.fact: The Connecticut River Scenic Farm Byway runs through Montague Center on Route 63 and Route 47.
The Massachusetts section begins at Routes 116 and 47 in South Hadley and was added to the national Connecticut River Byway on October 16, 2009.

Sunderland's Buttonball Tree is the largest American sycamore in Massachusetts and was alive when the U.S. Constitution was signed; Hadley has the most acreage of active farmland in the region, and the byway passes historic districts in Northfield, Montague Center, Sunderland, North Hadley and Hadley.

byways.review: Catalog road is the tri-state national byway; its MA portion (37.5 mapped miles) matches the MassDOT line (37.6 mi).

byways.name: Essex Coastal Scenic Byway
byways.where: About 90 miles of local roads and Routes 1A, 127 and 133 from Lynn to Salisbury through 14 coastal communities; Essex County

facts.fact: The 90-mile byway links 14 coastal communities from Lynn to Salisbury; Essex Heritage secured its state scenic byway designation.
In 1852 one out of every 28 American ships was built in one of Essex's 15 shipyards; the town has views of the Essex River and its marsh.
The byway passes the largest collection of remaining First Period houses in the country in Ipswich, roughly 59 homes.

byways.review: MassDOT layer names it 'Essex Heritage Scenic Byway'. Route numbers in 'where' are not from a fetched source except the general description; the catalog line covers only 23.5 mi in the northern part (Essex to Salisbury), while the MassDOT layer runs from Lynn (61.6 mi of centerline).

byways.name: Jacob's Ladder Trail
byways.where: US 20 from the Lee/Lenox line through Becket, Chester and Huntington to Russell; Berkshire, Hampden and Hampshire counties

facts.fact: The byway runs from Mt. Tekoa in Russell to the Lee/Lenox town line through Russell, Huntington, Chester, Becket and Lee, and was designated a Massachusetts Scenic Byway in 1992.
In 1910 as many as 4,000 people gathered on Morey Hill in Becket to mark the completion of the country's first auto road over a mountain range, and built a stone cairn at the 1,775-foot summit.
The byway is anchored by Tekoa Mountain in the east and Laurel Lake in the west; the Keystone Arches, mortarless stone railroad bridges of about 1840, stand in Middlefield, Becket and Chester.

byways.review: Wikipedia's US 20 article says the byway runs on into Westfield; MassDOT line ends near the Russell/Westfield line.

byways.name: Lost Villages Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Massachusetts Scenic Byway (also called the Route 122 Scenic Byway)
byways.where: Route 122 from Orange through New Salem, Petersham, Barre, Oakham and Rutland to Paxton; Franklin and Worcester counties

facts.fact: The Route 122 Scenic Byway links Orange and Paxton, passing north of the Quabbin Reservoir along 40 miles of back roads.
Four towns were relocated in the 1930s for the Quabbin project; in Petersham, Gate 40 leads to the former Dana town common and Gate 43 to the former town of Greenwich.
Route 122 North became a state scenic byway in 2007, a 40-mile corridor from Orange toward Worcester.

byways.review: Catalog line is 28.7 mi; MassDOT layer 36.3 mi; byway page says 40 miles.

byways.name: Minuteman Highway
byways.where: Route 2 (Concord Turnpike) from Cambridge through Arlington, Belmont, Lexington and Lincoln to the Concord Rotary; Middlesex County

facts.fact: MassDOT's byway map describes the Minuteman Highway as running parallel to and just south of the Battle Road scenic byway near Minute Man National Historical Park.

Route 2 between the Concord Rotary and Cambridge is a four-lane road through Concord and Lincoln and a six-lane freeway through Lexington, Belmont and Arlington; parts of it are known as the Cambridge and Concord Turnpike.

byways.review: Route identity inferred from the MassDOT line geometry (reverse-geocoded to Concord Turnpike, Cambridge to Concord Rotary). No official page or designation document found.

byways.name: Mohawk Trail
byways.designation: Massachusetts Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway (FHWA, 2021)
byways.where: Route 2 and Route 2A from Williamstown through North Adams, Charlemont, Shelburne, Greenfield and Erving to Orange and Athol; Berkshire, Franklin and Worcester counties

facts.fact: The Mohawk Trail officially opened on October 22, 1914, and is called the first scenic road in New England.
The trail began as a Native American trade route; Route 2 crosses the Connecticut on the French King Bridge 140 feet up and reaches 2,272 feet at Whitcomb Summit.
The 69-mile byway descends after the hairpin turn at Clarksburg into the Hoosic River valley at North Adams.
FHWA lists the Mohawk Trail Scenic Byway as a National Scenic Byway of 69 miles.

byways.review: FHWA national id 81504; catalog id 2585 is the older state record. Catalog line runs to the New York line and so overlaps the Taconic Trail.

byways.name: Mount Greylock Scenic Byway
byways.where: Rockwell Road and Notch Road through Mount Greylock State Reservation, Lanesborough to North Adams; Berkshire County

facts.fact: The byway runs from farmland in Lanesborough through Mount Greylock State Reservation to North Adams; the 3,491-foot summit carries the 1932 War Memorial Tower and the CCC-built Bascom Lodge.
The parkway through the reservation is open to vehicles from late May through mid-October.
A 2008-2009 Historic Parkway Rehabilitation Project restored the reservation's roads along the state-designated scenic byway.

byways.review: DCR's mass.gov page for the reservation (https://www.mass.gov/locations/mount-greylock-state-reservation) returns 403 to scripted fetches and could not be checked.

byways.name: Old King's Highway
byways.designation: Massachusetts Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway (FHWA, 2021)
byways.where: Route 6A from Bourne through Sandwich, Barnstable, Yarmouth, Dennis and Brewster to Orleans; Barnstable County

facts.fact: Route 6A runs through eight National Register districts past early Cape Cod houses, sea captains' homes and Victorian buildings, with bayside marsh views and cranberry bogs; the byway is 34 miles.
The national byway runs from Sandwich Road and US 6 in Bourne to Route 6A and US 6 in Orleans and was designated February 16, 2021.
Most of Route 6A is known as the Old King's Highway; the Barnstable portion is listed on the National Register as the Old King's Highway Historic District.

byways.review: Official page is the FHWA America's Byways entry; the local oldkingshighway.org site did not respond.

byways.name: Route 112 Scenic Byway
byways.where: Route 112 from the Vermont line at Colrain through Shelburne, Buckland, Ashfield, Goshen, Cummington and Worthington to Huntington; Franklin and Hampshire counties

facts.fact: The byway runs from the Vermont border in Colrain to Huntington past working farms, farm stands and honor-system roadside tables.
The east branch of the Wild and Scenic Westfield River parallels Route 112 through much of its southern half.
Shelburne Falls' Bridge of Flowers blooms from April tulips to October chrysanthemums; William Cullen Bryant's boyhood home is in Cummington.

byways.name: Route 116 Scenic Byway
byways.where: Route 116 from Adams through Cheshire, Savoy, Plainfield, Ashfield and Conway to South Deerfield; Berkshire and Franklin counties

facts.fact: The byway runs between Adams at its western end and South Deerfield at its eastern end, through Ashfield near the junction with Route 112.
A Cheshire monument recalls the town's 1802 gift to President Jefferson of a 1,234-pound wheel of cheese.
The 1870 Burkeville covered bridge in Conway was restored in 2005 for walkers and cyclists.

byways.review: Not in the Rambleroo catalog; draw from the MassDOT layer.

byways.name: Taconic Trail
byways.where: Route 2 from US 7 in Williamstown west to Petersburg Pass at the New York line; Berkshire County

facts.fact: Route 2 begins at Petersburg Pass on the New York line and is known as the Taconic Trail west of Route 7 in Williamstown.
MassDOT's byway map describes it as a short route through Taconic Trail State Forest to New York.
Across the line, New York Route 2 carries the Taconic Trail name through the wooded Taconic Mountains in Petersburgh.

byways.review: No official page found. Catalog's Mohawk Trail line already includes this stretch to the state line.

issues: No current mass.gov page listing the byways was found; mass.gov returns 403 to both curl and WebFetch, so a page may exist and was not checked. The program list rests on the MassDOT GIS layer and its 2018 map PDF, which agree with Scenic America's 14-road list.

Catalog designations are stale for three roads: FHWA lists the Battle Road (81503), Mohawk Trail (81504) and Old King's Highway (81505) as National Scenic Byways designated February 16, 2021; the catalog marks them state-only. Wikipedia and Scenic America call the Battle Road an All-American Road, but FHWA's own page labels it National Scenic Byway.

Essex Coastal Scenic Byway catalog line covers only 23.5 mi (Essex to Salisbury); the byway is about 90 miles from Lynn to Salisbury and the MassDOT layer (as 'Essex Heritage Scenic Byway') runs from Lynn. Consider drawing from the layer.
Lost Villages catalog line is 28.7 mi against 36.3 mi in the MassDOT layer and 40 miles in the byway's own description.
Catalog Mohawk Trail line extends west to the New York line and so includes the separately designated Taconic Trail; the MassDOT Mohawk Trail line ends in Williamstown and runs east to Athol.
Minuteman Highway: no designation document or official page found; identification as Route 2 between Cambridge and the Concord Rotary comes from the MassDOT line and map text.
Lost Villages Scenic Byway is called the Route 122 Scenic Byway on bywayswestmass.com; the Blackstone Canal Heritage Highway is also Route 122, further south. Do not merge them.
